title: Coroner's inquest slated in 2016 death of man who spent night in Saanich police cells
subtitle: An inquest will be held in the death of a Victoria man who died after spending a night in Saanich police cells, the B.C. Coroners Service said Friday. Andre Claude Boucher, 60, died in August 2016.
article: An inquest will be held in the death of a Victoria man who died after spending a night in Saanich police cells, the B.C. Coroners Service said Friday.
Andre Claude Boucher, 60, died in August 2016.
He was placed in Saanich police cells on the evening of July 27, 2016.
Shortly after 10 a.m. the next day, paramedics were called to assess Boucher.
He was taken to Victoria General Hospital, where he died in early August.
A Saanich police spokesman said officers were originally responding to a report of a man being intoxicated in public.
The inquest will take place May 14 at the Victoria courthouse. It is being held because Boucher was in police custody when he became unresponsive.
A B.C. Coroners Service inquest is a fact-finding mission in which a jury hears sworn testimony. It does not determine guilt or fault.
Afterward, the jury can recommend procedural changes or measures to prevent future, similar deaths.
